clue.text: Model I clad in copper and non-metallic material

indicators.note: to be clad in something is to be wrapped by it, so the copper surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
a last is a shoemaker's model of a foot

explanation.surface: A figure of me dressed in copper alongside some non-metal stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastics are synthetic substances containing no metal, a common manufactured material.

clue.text: First indication of price cut, thank goodness!

indicators.note: the first indication of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A shopper relieved at the first sign of a price reduction.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of relief, the same feeling as saying thank goodness.

clue.text: Where our editor is, loosely speaking? Not always

definitions.text: Where our editor is, loosely speaking?
definitions.meaning: the puzzle's editor works at The Times, said loosely by dropping the article

explanation.definitionFit: Something done only on occasion is done not always but sometimes.

clue.text: Volunteers confronting 'orsy country pursuit sneer

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve of volunteer soldiers

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of a Cockney saying horsey shows the H falls from the word

parts.note: hunting, a hunt, is a traditional British country pursuit

explanation.surface: Volunteers face a horsey rural sport with contempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orsy is horsy as a Cockney says it, dropping the aitch, which tells you what the country pursuit loses; 'confronting' just means standing in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to jeer at someone, much as a sneer mocks.

clue.text: Person taking legal action? One may come in crying out

indicators.note: one piece entering another, so the I goes inside

parts.note: clamant means noisily crying out or demanding
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A litigant, someone who might arrive shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant brings a claim, the plaintiff in a lawsuit.

clue.text: Ruler's beautiful love letter read out

definitions.note: the 's stands for is: the ruler is the answer

indicators.note: spoken aloud, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: beautiful gives FAIR, and the letter that means love (nil in tennis) is O

explanation.surface: A monarch's fine romantic note being recited.
explanation.definitionFit: The kings of ancient Egypt bore this title as their supreme sovereigns.

clue.text: Wander up with cooked dish for Frenchman

parts.note: a pie is a cooked dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: to err is to wander or stray

explanation.surface: A Frenchman strolling about with a cooked meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical male French first name standing for any Frenchman.

clue.text: Playwright can generate extremes of hilarity in funny clauses

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes inside the rearranged word
funny suggests something odd, so the letters are rearranged
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dramatist manages to raise laughs from comic phrases.
explanation.walkthrough: HY, the ends of 'hilarity', goes inside AESCLUS, made from 'clauses' by 'funny'.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek tragedian who wrote the Oresteia.

clue.text: Nymph shortly getting up with the sun, in the mist?

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the word upwards, backwards
cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: an oread is a mountain nymph
Sol is the sun, Latin and astronomical

explanation.surface: A nymph rising at dawn in the morning haze.
explanation.walkthrough: OREAD loses D for OREA, which 'getting up' turns to AERO.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray from a can is a fine mist of droplets suspended in gas.

clue.text: It's endlessly difficult to get maiden into agreement —— bother!

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: hard means difficult

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for agreement

parts.note: assent is agreement
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Frustration that it is hard to get a girl to agree.
explanation.definitionFit: Persistent pestering or troubling of someone is a form of being bothered.

clue.text: Train excursion curtailed — there's anger about that

indicators.note: around, so the anger word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to enrage is to anger

indicators.note: cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: a tour is an excursion

explanation.surface: A railway trip cut short causes fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is not a railway but a retinue, as in a royal train.
explanation.definitionFit: A train of followers is the retinue or attendants of an important person.

clue.text: Maybe batsman missing a century will become more upset

indicators.note: without, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: a batsman, for example, is someone who scores runs
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricketer who falls short of a hundred runs will be more unhappy.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a century is a hundred runs, which fits the surface; here it is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore can mean aggrieved, so the comparative form means feeling more aggrieved.

clue.text: Transformation that could be effected by smarties with oomph

indicators.note: the change in the surface also means the letters can be rearranged to make the word

explanation.surface: A change brought about by energetic clever people.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete change of form, as a caterpillar into a butterfly.

clue.text: Irresponsible type getting the most generous happy-hour offer?

definitions.meaning: a person who lives without conventional constraints
the best bar deal would be a shot of liquor at no charge

explanation.definitionFit: A person who is independent and carefree, ignoring convention and duty.

clue.text: Decree to restrict street crime in the Wild West

indicators.note: the decree word confines the other piece inside it

parts.note: a ruling is a decree

explanation.surface: An edict to curb street lawlessness on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing cattle or horses was the classic outlaw offence of the American frontier.

clue.text: Short hair on ladies unnaturally constrained?

indicators.note: shortened, losing its final letter

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

indicators.note: not in their natural order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Women's cropped hair looking oddly restricted.
explanation.walkthrough: LOC (from LOCK) is followed by ALISED, 'ladies' rearranged by 'unnaturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something confined to one particular area has been restricted in extent.

clue.text: In close by using some force, look at this race

indicators.note: the short word goes inside the other

parts.note: to slam is to shut forcefully
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A forceful shutting, then look at this contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A downhill ski race weaving between gates is a competition of speed.

clue.text: Hello, the thing dunked in strong drink is mushroom!

indicators.note: plunged into a liquid, so the pieces go inside

parts.note: sake is a strong Japanese rice wine
hi is a greeting
it means the thing

explanation.surface: A greeting at finding something dipped in liquor turns out to be fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese edible fungus grown on logs, widely used in cooking.

clue.text: Hope for lover of yesteryear to get kissed, we hear

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: as heard aloud, so the sound of the word is used

parts.note: pecked means kissed lightly

explanation.surface: Wishing for an old flame to give a peck.
explanation.definitionFit: To anticipate something likely, much like hoping it will come.

clue.text: Motorway up? Stick around, or find diversion

indicators.note: the stick word goes round the other piece

parts.note: paste is glue, something that sticks

indicators.note: in a down clue, up reads the letters backwards

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written MI

explanation.surface: The motorway is closed, wait about or take a detour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' suggests a road detour, but it means amusement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or amusement is a pleasant diversion from work.

clue.text: Nazi male in prison —— perhaps a castle?

indicators.note: placed inside the prison word

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
Rudolf Hess was a leading Nazi

explanation.surface: A Nazi man jailed, maybe in a fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: Hess was in fact imprisoned, so the surface rings true; castle is the chess rook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rook, also called a castle, is one of the pieces in chess.

clue.text: As young girl, I have intelligence in this?

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A young woman claims she has brains.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter carries information, the intelligence it bears.

clue.text: Tiger maybe sitting on grass in a poetic land

parts.note: a tiger is an example of a big cat
hay is dried grass

explanation.surface: A tiger lying on grass in a lyrical country.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting on' puts CAT above HAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary name for China used by poets.

clue.text: Timid miaul with lion sadly turning into much tamer feline?

indicators.note: going inside, so the jumbled letters enter the cat word

parts.note: a puss is a domestic cat, far tamer than a lion

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lion's feeble mew means it has become a mere moggy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a lion's pathetic mew shrinking it to a house cat; 'sadly' is the anagram signal and 'turning into' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearful and lacking courage, cowardly.

clue.text: Very gallant gentleman speaks, abandoning shelter finally

indicators.note: giving up, so a letter is removed

parts.note: orates means speaks formally

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A brave man talking as he leaves his tent at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Oates walked out of Scott's Antarctic tent to die; his epitaph calls him a very gallant gentleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawrence Oates, Scott's polar companion, whose memorial bears that phrase.

clue.text: Hide as son not getting on with relations

indicators.note: lacking, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A boy hiding because he does not get on with his family.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin.

clue.text: Restrictions imposed by rules not good

indicators.note: without, so the letter is omitted

parts.note: a monarch reigns, that is rules

explanation.surface: Curbs set by regulations are no good.
explanation.definitionFit: Reins are controls that restrain, figuratively restrictions.

clue.text: His racket gets thrown down

indicators.note: thrown suggests tossed about, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A tennis player hurls his racket to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' looks like where the racket is thrown, but it is the definition, meaning sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means low in spirits, despondent.

clue.text: Period of grace initially at the maternity hospital?

definitions.text: Period of grace initially at the maternity hospital?

parts.words: Period of grace initially at the maternity hospital
parts.note: in the nursery rhyme, the child born on this weekday is full of grace

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Monday's child is fair of face' continues with the next day's child being full of grace.
explanation.definitionFit: A day of the week, the one the rhyme links with being full of grace.

clue.text: Possibly Japanese festival beginning in Nagasaki

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival

indicators.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A festival may be starting in a Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Japan is in the Far East, so something Japanese is oriental.
